newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS NOT EXPECTED AT IMOLA TRIAL OPENING.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS NOT EXPECTED AT IMOLA TRIAL OPENING.

text.p: Frank Williams is not expected to travel to Imola next week to appear on the opening day of the trial at which he faces culpable homicide charges associated with Ayrton Senna's death at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix.

This unexpected change to Williams' original plans was confirmed on Wednesday when a team spokesman said that Williams, his technical director Patrick Head and chief designer Adrian Newey had been advised not to attend.

In a brief statement, the team said: "Obviously, the Williams team personnel will be appearing at the trial. However, we have been in discussions with our legal team and they advised us it is not necessary for Williams' personnel to be present on Thursday, February 20."
Williams had said previously that he would be going to Imola for the trial opening because he felt it was right for him to be seen to be representing his team.

But a reliable source close to the Williams team said it was now understood that the opening day of the trial would revolve solely around the procedural interests of the lawyers. Williams' presence, said the source, would only attract a media circus.

After the trial starts on February 20, it will continue on isolated days thereafter, with the next likely day of activity expected to be on February 28. It is anticipated the trial will last for at least six months.

Williams, Head, Newey, race director Roland Bruynseraede of Belgium, Imola circuit director Giorgio Poggi and race organiser Federico Bendinelli all face charges of culpable homicide in relation to Senna's death, at the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola, on May 1, 1994.
